tests.name: it.each([['new frontend system', 'Link: [pending]', 'Link: [/new-page]'], ['legacy', 'Link: []', 'Link: [/legacy-page]']])('should resolve %s route refs in app root elements across finalization', async (hook, bootstrapText, finalizedText) => ...)
tests.given: In the test body: `newPageRouteRef = createRouteRef()`, `legacyPageRouteRef = createLegacyRouteRef({ id: 'legacy-page' })`; `NewLink` renders `useRouteRef(newPageRouteRef)?.() ?? 'pending'` and `LegacyLink` renders `useLegacyRouteRef(legacyPageRouteRef)()`, both as `Link: [${link}]`; `LinkElement = hook === 'legacy' ? LegacyLink : NewLink`. `prepareSpecializedApp` with the describe-level `appPlugin`, a `createFrontendModule({ pluginId: 'app' })` holding the capturing `sign-in-page:app` override, and `createFrontendPlugin({ pluginId: 'test', routes: { newPage: newPageRouteRef, legacyPage: legacyPageRouteRef } })` with `PageBlueprint.make` pages `new-page` (path '/new-page', routeRef newPageRouteRef, loader rendering 'New Page') and `legacy-page` (path '/legacy-page', routeRef legacyPageRouteRef, loader rendering 'Legacy Page') and `AppRootElementBlueprint.make({ name: 'link', params: { element: <LinkElement /> } })`. Render `<PreparedAppRoot preparedApp={preparedApp} />`, a component declared in the test body as `function PreparedAppRoot(props: { preparedApp: PreparedSpecializedApp })` with `useState<FinalizedSpecializedApp>()`, `useEffect(() => props.preparedApp.onFinalized(setFinalizedApp), [props.preparedApp])`, returning `finalizedApp?.element ?? props.preparedApp.getBootstrapApp().element` (the same swap as createApp.tsx, so root elements stay mounted).
tests.expect: 'Custom Sign In' and `bootstrapText` are found during bootstrap. After `finalizedAppPromise = waitForFinalizedApp(preparedApp)`, the sign-in trigger in `act`, and `await act(async () => { await finalizedAppPromise; })`: 'App Layout' is found, `finalizedText` is found, and `bootstrapText` is no longer in the document. Before the fix the legacy row fails during bootstrap (the hook throws and the boundary renders nothing) and the new-system row fails after finalization (it stays 'Link: [pending]').

tests.name: should re-resolve app root element route refs across finalization after a bootstrap error
tests.given: `errorRouteRef = createLegacyRouteRef({ id: 'error-route' })`; `rejectingPermissionApiRef = createApiRef<{ authorize(): Promise<never> }>({ id: 'plugin.permission.api' })`. Features: `noSignInAppPlugin`; `createFrontendPlugin({ pluginId: 'test', routes: { errorRoute: errorRouteRef } })` with a `createExtension({ name: 'deferred-route', attachTo: { id: 'app/root', input: 'elements' }, if: { permissions: { $contains: 'test.permission' } }, output: [coreExtensionData.reactElement, coreExtensionData.routePath, coreExtensionData.routeRef] })` yielding `<div />`, '/error-route' and errorRouteRef, plus `AppRootElementBlueprint.make({ name: 'link' })` whose element renders `useLegacyRouteRef(errorRouteRef)()` as `Link: [${link}]`; and `createFrontendModule({ pluginId: 'app' })` with `ApiBlueprint.make({ name: 'permission' })` defining `rejectingPermissionApiRef` with `deps: {}` and a factory whose `authorize` is `async () => { throw new Error('Permission backend unavailable'); }`. Before rendering: `api = preparedApp.getBootstrapApp().apis.get(routeResolutionApiRef)!`, `listener = jest.fn()`, `api.onFinalized?.(listener)`. At the start of the test body, a short comment says why the route sits under `app/root.elements` and why the test stays on the bootstrap render: page routes are not built on this path, and in a real app the app root error boundary replaces the root elements.
tests.expect: Right after `getBootstrapApp()` (the startup initialize), `api.isFinalized?.()` is `false` and `listener` was not called. `renderPreparedBootstrap(preparedApp)` shows 'Link: []'. After `await act(async () => { await waitForFinalizedApp(preparedApp); })`, `listener` was called exactly once, `api.isFinalized?.()` is `true`, and 'Link: [/error-route]' is found in the still-mounted bootstrap render.

tests.name: should signal route resolution finalization once across finalization when the error path follows normal finalization
tests.given: `let appRootCalls = 0`; `prepareSpecializedApp({ features: [noSignInAppPlugin], advanced: { extensionFactoryMiddleware(originalFactory, { node }) { ... } } })` where the middleware increments `appRootCalls` when `node.spec.id === 'app/root'`, throws `new Error('Finalization failure')` when that count reaches 2 (the normal finalization pass), and otherwise returns `originalFactory()`. Then `api = preparedApp.getBootstrapApp().apis.get(routeResolutionApiRef)!`, `listener = jest.fn()`, `api.onFinalized?.(listener)`. No React render.
tests.expect: Before finalizing, `api.isFinalized?.()` is `false` and `listener` was not called. After `const finalizedApp = await waitForFinalizedApp(preparedApp)`: `appRootCalls` is 3 (bootstrap, failed normal finalization, bootstrap-error finalization), `finalizedApp.errors` is `undefined` (the bootstrap-error app), `listener` was called exactly once, and `api.isFinalized?.()` is `true`.

tests.name: should re-resolve once across finalization and not re-render for APIs without finalization support
tests.given: A mock API with `let finalized = false`, `listeners = new Set<() => void>()`, `resolve: jest.fn(() => (finalized ? () => '/ready' : undefined))`, `isFinalized: () => finalized`, `onFinalized: listener => { listeners.add(listener); return () => { listeners.delete(listener); }; }`, rendered with a render counter; then a second hook rendered against `{ resolve: jest.fn(() => () => '/plain') }` with its own counter, plus a third hook mounted against a fresh API built the same way (its own listener set) and unmounted before any signal.
tests.expect: Mounted in bootstrap: result is `undefined`, `resolve` called once, 1 render, 1 listener. After `act(() => { finalized = true; listeners.forEach(l => l()); })`: `result.current?.()` is '/ready', `resolve` called twice, exactly 2 renders, and the listener set is empty. The plain API: result returns '/plain', 1 render, `resolve` called once after `await act(async () => {})`. The third hook had one listener while mounted and its listener set is empty after `unmount()`.

tests.name: should not miss a finalization that happens while subscribing across finalization
tests.given: Mock API A: `let finalized = false`, `isFinalized: jest.fn(() => finalized)`, `onFinalized: jest.fn(() => { finalized = true; return () => {}; })` (finalizes during subscription without calling the listener), `resolve: jest.fn(() => (finalized ? () => '/ready' : undefined))`. Mock API B: `isFinalized: () => true`, `onFinalized: jest.fn()`, `resolve: jest.fn(() => () => '/done')`. Each rendered with a render counter.
tests.expect: A: `onFinalized` was called once and `result.current?.()` is '/ready' after the effects flush, with at most 2 renders. B (finalized at mount): `onFinalized` was never called, `result.current?.()` is '/done', exactly 1 render.
